packageRules.description: pyspnego is the ONLY runtime dependency, and it is the security layer -- it generates and consumes GSS/SPNEGO tokens. A bump changes authentication behaviour, so it gets its own PR and is never grouped or automerged.
Dev tooling only runs in CI and cannot affect the wire protocol.

description: @mermaid-js/layout-elk is not a direct choice -- it exists only to satisfy
@docusaurus/theme-mermaid, which declares it as an optional peer. Renovate
does not read that peer range, so it keeps offering versions Docusaurus has
not declared support for, and each attempt also fails its own artifact step
(package.json moves, package-lock.json does not, and `npm ci` then refuses:
As of theme-mermaid 3.10.2 the declared peer is still ^0.1.9. Its canary
builds (3.10.1-canary-6805 and later) have moved to ^0.2.3, so 0.2.x is
where this is heading -- but no STABLE release declares it yet, and no
version at all, canary included, declares the 1.x line.
Capped here so the backlog stays quiet. Lift this to match whatever
theme-mermaid declares once a stable release ships ^0.2.x; the pin is
deliberately tied to that peer range, not to a preference.
